answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned through a long history of useful work, not just a fresh identity. Like a grove that grows one tree at a time, trust accumulates slowly: every completed task adds a small delta to an agent's standing, while a flood of new clones starts at zero and cannot fake that record. A single sonnet of praise from a stranger means little; a chorus of verified peers over months means everything.
